# pai memory

Search and index your notes and memory files

```
pai memory <command>
```

The memory index makes notes and memory files searchable. `pai memory search` is the one you want most days.

```sh
pai memory search "release checklist"
pai memory status
pai memory index
```

See also: `pai find`, `pai kg`, `pai zettel`

### pai memory search

Search what the memory index knows

```
pai memory search QUERY [options]
```

Finds notes and memory files that match a query: by keywords (default), by meaning (semantic), or both (hybrid). Results are re-ranked unless you turn that off, and recent items get a boost if you ask for one.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `QUERY` | yes | What to look for |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--project SLUG` | string | — | Only this project |
| `--source KIND` | string | — | Only 'memory' files or only 'notes' |
| `--limit N` | number | — | Maximum results (default from `pai memory settings`) |
| `--mode MODE` | string | — | keyword (default), semantic or hybrid |
| `--no-rerank` | flag | — | Skip the second ranking pass (faster, a little less precise) |
| `--recency DAYS` | number | — | Boost recent results: the score halves every DAYS days; 0 = off |

```sh
pai memory search "release checklist"
pai memory search "retry loop" --project my-project --mode hybrid
pai memory search deploy --no-rerank --limit 5
```

See also: `pai memory settings`, `pai find`

### pai memory status

How much the memory index holds

```
pai memory status [PROJECT]
```

Shows the storage backend and the number of indexed files and chunks. For live counts per project use `pai daemon status`.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT` | no | Show this project only |

```sh
pai memory status
pai memory status my-project
```

See also: `pai memory sources`, `pai daemon status`

### pai memory index

Read project notes and memory files into the search index

```
pai memory index [PROJECT] [options]
```

Reads the notes and memory files of one project, or of all active projects, into the search index so `pai memory search` can find them. If the background service is running and no project is named, it is asked to do the work; otherwise it runs here.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT` | no | Index only this project (default: all active projects) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--all` | flag | — | All active projects (this is the default when no project is named) |
| `--embed` | flag | — | Also compute the meaning vectors for new text, so semantic search can use it |
| `--direct` | flag | — | Do not ask the background service; run here (for debugging) |
| `--background` | flag | — | Run at low priority (implies --direct) |

```sh
pai memory index
pai memory index my-project --embed
pai memory index --background
```

See also: `pai memory embed`, `pai memory status`

### pai memory embed

Compute meaning vectors for indexed text that has none yet

```
pai memory embed [PROJECT] [options]
```

Semantic and hybrid search need a vector per text chunk. This fills in the missing ones, in batches; safe to stop and re-run.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT` | no | Only this project (default: all) |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--batch-size N` | number | 25 | Chunks to compute per batch |
| `--max-minutes N` | number | 60 | Stop cleanly after this many minutes; run again to continue |
| `--all` | flag | — | No time budget: run until the whole backlog is embedded |
| `--background` | flag | — | Run at low priority so the computer stays responsive |

```sh
pai memory embed
pai memory embed my-project --batch-size 20
pai memory embed --max-minutes 10
pai memory embed --all
```

See also: `pai memory index`, `pai memory backend detect`

### pai memory settings

Show or change the search settings

```
pai memory settings [KEY] [VALUE]
```

With no arguments, lists the search settings (mode, rerank, recencyBoostDays, defaultLimit, snippetLength). With a key, prints its value; with a key and a value, saves it to the PAI config file.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `KEY` | no | Setting name |
| `VALUE` | no | New value |

```sh
pai memory settings
pai memory settings mode
pai memory settings mode hybrid
```

See also: `pai config path`

### pai memory sources

Where the indexed content comes from

```
pai memory sources [options]
```

Shows what the indexer has taken in: composition by source, which roots content enters from, the heaviest single files, and how many chunks are rewritten per day (which tells a finite backlog from a treadmill).

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--limit N` | number | 8 | Rows per section |

```sh
pai memory sources
pai memory sources --limit 20
```

See also: `pai memory status`

### pai memory backend

Embedding backends: detect, use, provision

```
pai memory backend <command>
```

An index is bound to the backend that embedded it. Pick a backend here; switching an existing index also needs `pai memory reembed`.

```sh
pai memory backend detect
pai memory backend use ollama
```

See also: `pai memory reembed`

#### pai memory backend detect

Check which embedding backends work here

```
pai memory backend detect
```

Probes the available embedding backends (ollama, then transformers-cpu) and recommends the fastest.

```sh
pai memory backend detect
pai memory backend use ollama
```

See also: `pai memory backend use`

#### pai memory backend use

Choose the embedding backend

```
pai memory backend use ID [options]
```

Writes the backend to the config. It does not touch the index; an index that already holds vectors from another backend needs `pai memory reembed`.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ID` | yes | Backend id, e.g. ollama or transformers-cpu-q8 |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--model NAME` | string | — | Model name on that backend |

```sh
pai memory backend use ollama
pai memory backend use transformers-cpu-q8 --model my-model
```

See also: `pai memory backend detect`, `pai memory reembed`

#### pai memory backend provision

Download and set up a backend's model

```
pai memory backend provision BACKEND
```

Only ollama needs this: it downloads the embedding model file and registers it with ollama.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `BACKEND` | yes | Backend to set up (only: ollama) |

```sh
pai memory backend provision ollama
pai memory backend use ollama
```

See also: `pai memory backend use`

### pai memory reembed

Switch the index to another embedding backend

```
pai memory reembed [options]
```

Clears every stored vector (in batches, resumable) so the index can be refilled by the new backend with `pai memory embed`. Keyword search keeps working meanwhile. Without --yes it only prints the plan and refuses.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--backend ID` | string | — | Target backend (default: the configured one); also written to the config |
| `--yes` | flag | — | Go ahead; without it only the plan is printed |

```sh
pai memory reembed
pai memory reembed --backend ollama --yes
```

See also: `pai memory embed`, `pai memory backend use`

### pai memory pass

Internal: one background pass started by the daemon

```
pai memory pass NAME [options]
```

Used by the background service to run an index or embed pass at low priority and report one JSON line. Not meant to be typed.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NAME` | yes | index, embed or noop |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--sleep MS` | number | 0 | noop pass only: sleep this many milliseconds |
| `--max-minutes N` | number | — | embed pass only: time budget in minutes |
| `--max-load N` | number | — | embed pass only: yield above this load average |

```sh
pai memory pass noop --sleep 10
pai memory pass index
```

## Subcommands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `pai memory search` | Search what the memory index knows |
| `pai memory status` | How much the memory index holds |
| `pai memory index` | Read project notes and memory files into the search index |
| `pai memory embed` | Compute meaning vectors for indexed text that has none yet |
| `pai memory settings` | Show or change the search settings |
| `pai memory sources` | Where the indexed content comes from |
| `pai memory backend` | Embedding backends: detect, use, provision |
| `pai memory reembed` | Switch the index to another embedding backend |
| `pai memory pass` | Internal: one background pass started by the daemon |

## Examples

```bash
# Search federated memory across all projects
pai memory search "cross-encoder reranker"

# Semantic (vector) search with recency boost (reranking is on by default)
pai memory search "token factory" --mode semantic --recency 90

# Re-index a project's memory/ and Notes/ directories
pai memory index

# Show index size and embedding coverage
pai memory status
```
